author: kingpanther13
releaseNotes:
v5.1.1 - 2026-10-30
- feat: rebuild hub_update_device on the device page's native saves (#567)
  - `hub_update_device` now takes `fields` and `preferences`: put device settings such as label, room, tags or showOnHome inside `fields`. `hub_get_device(mode='configuration')` lists every field with its type, current value and whether the device offers it.
    - Device Info changes save in one request and preferences in another, the way the device page saves them; mixed updates are about twice as fast.
    - `room` accepts a room name or id; a number is always an id, and text matches a name first.
    - Settings that already had the requested value are reported as `unchanged` instead of as changes.
  - `hub_create_device` sets the requested label as part of creating the device.
  - New setting: Hide passwords and credentials in MCP responses (ON by default). Turn it off to let the AI read stored passwords and credential-named values.
    - A hidden value sent back in an update is refused, so the stored password or code is never overwritten.
    - More names count as credentials (PINs and codes such as `userPin`, `alarmCode`, `installerCode`), and Rule Machine local variables and device preferences and data named that way (`doorCode`, `alarmPin`) are hidden too.
  - `hub_get_rule_health` reports an unknown app id as not found.
  - `hub_get_app_config` shows each setting's saved value on the page instead of the app's default.
  - Dashboard PINs are hidden while Hide passwords and credentials is on; updating a dashboard from a read keeps its PIN.

v5.1.0 - 2026-10-29
- feat: rebuild hub_set_native_app on the native form engine (#563)
  - Native apps: `hub_set_native_app` now works like `hub_set_rule`: create an app, update its fields, or step through its own pages (`operation` create, update, form). It covers every built-in classic app and user or community apps too. The old parameter names are gone; the tool explains its three operations when called without one. Inputs you leave unset keep their page defaults, a sub-page can be edited in one call, and a refused create leaves nothing behind.
  - Removed tool: `hub_list_app_pages`. Its job moved into `hub_get_app_config`, whose result now lists the pages a page links to under `page.hrefs`; read the default page first and pass a linked page as `pageName`.
  - `hub_get_app_config` with `includeSettings` now hides password values on every page of an app and settings whose names look like credentials. OAuth access tokens follow the "Hide access tokens in MCP responses" setting and are always hidden from per-client tokens.
  - Backups: pre-edit snapshots no longer store password-typed settings; a restore keeps the live password in place and tells you which passwords to re-enter when an app is recreated. When the backup storage budget is full, the oldest backups are removed first and the newest backup of each app or rule is always kept; the "Prioritize the first snapshot when pruning backups" setting is now "Take a fresh snapshot before every edit", which is what it did.
  - Rule Machine: `hub_set_rule` refuses a batch that deletes or edits a row it already deleted before any change, and accepts retargeting an IF and deleting its old condition in one batch; `hub_call_rule` start/stop messages describe exactly what Rule Machine does.
